---
title: "How to Watch a Broadcast Like You Mean It"
subtitle: "What the TV camera hides, what the replays and the All-22 give back, the five-second read before every snap, your first tells, and the prediction log you'll keep for the rest of the course."
description: "How a football broadcast is built and what it leaves out; the sideline, end-zone and skycam angles; All-22 coaches film; reading the scorebug in five seconds; win probability and Next Gen Stats as glossed numbers; the 'watch one thing' strategy; a starter catalogue of tells (stance, the back's depth and offset, receiver splits, safety depth); and a prediction log, on paper and in ten lines of pandas, scored against what the situation alone would get you."
glossary:
  "Sideline camera": "The broadcast's main camera, high on one side of the field near midfield. It follows the ball with a fairly tight shot, which is good for the ball and the faces and poor for the safeties and the receivers away from the ball."
  "End-zone camera": "A camera behind one end zone, looking straight down the field. It shows the blocking, the gaps between linemen and the running lanes better than any other angle; coaches film includes a high version of it."
  "Skycam": "A camera hung from cables above the field that can fly anywhere over it, usually just behind the offense. It shows roughly the quarterback's view of the defense: the coverage, the safeties and the routes."
  "All-22": "Game film shot from high above the sideline and zoomed out so that all 22 players stay in the frame for the whole play, with no cut-aways. The standard view for studying a game."
  "Coaches film": "The video a team's staff studies: every snap shown twice, once from the high wide sideline angle (the All-22) and once from a high end-zone angle, with no replays, close-ups or graphics. Fans can buy access to it."
  "Tell": "A detail before the snap that leaks what a player or team is about to do, such as a lineman's stance or a safety's depth. A clue that shifts the odds, never a guarantee."
  "Stance (two-point / three-point)": "How a player stands just before the snap. In a two-point stance he is upright, with only his feet on the ground; in a three-point stance one hand is also on the ground (a four-point stance puts both hands down)."
  "Heavy hand": {def: "A three-point stance with a lot of the lineman's weight leaning on his down hand (shoulders forward, knuckles pressing white). It usually means he is about to fire forward to run-block; a light hand, with the weight back on the heels, suggests he is about to step back into a pass set.", aliases: ["Heavy stance"]}
  "Prediction log": "Your running record of pre-snap calls: for each snap, the situation, your guess (run or pass, later more), how confident you were, the main clue, and what actually happened. Scored to see whether your reading is getting better."
---
